hook: Cryptosporidium's single rhoptry keeps secreting after invasion, then becomes the feeder organelle
summary: The diarrhea-causing parasite Cryptosporidium releases its secretory organelles in sequence to anchor itself before entering a gut cell. Its one rhoptry keeps pushing out waves of effector proteins, and its membrane later forms the feeder organelle that divides host and parasite. This comes from high-resolution imaging with molecular markers in cultured cells, so the model still needs testing in infected animals.
title: The single Cryptosporidium rhoptry sequentially drives invasion and host-parasite interface formation.
